symptom: The linked BUY and local outcome race parity entry points accepted a successful lower-level cross-ledger preflight but then read original caller-controlled candidate/decision/outcome objects. A reference Proxy trap could alter race membership or refund disposition after the lower-level snapshot, making unequal or excluded race sets appear aligned (never granting scoring).
lesson: Successful validation of a detached lower-level copy does not protect a higher-level parity check that later consumes original caller references. A late cross-input mutation can change the apparent cohort or exclusion classification after preflight.
guardrail: Pin candidate, references, decisions and outcomes into one set of bounded detached input graphs before calling lower-level preflight and use only those same pinned graphs for linked BUY and local outcome race-set parity. Preserve refund/exclusion asymmetry as a denial, assert late mutation triggers, and never infer independent settlement or scoring authority.
